Independent bounded replay at B=1: enumerate subsets of rho edges and retain those that are acyclic by union–find (thus spanning trees); accumulate each product and each derivative by omitting the differentiated edge factor, including the derivative at zero shortcut. For lengths (2,3), (2,2,2), (2,2,2,3), and (3,4,5,6,7), the direct log-det derivatives were respectively 4, 4, 5.026334038989729, and 21 to rounding, versus rho=4,4,6,21. Positive-edge derivative deviations were below 7e-12 and budget errors below 1e-12. The strict deletion case gave xi=1.193712943361397.
correctness.rationale: A tree retains exactly one complete terminal path (possibly the direct edge); every other long path must lose exactly one edge to avoid cycles without isolating internal vertices. This gives the multiaffine path polynomial even at zero weights. A positive design exists, and on the positive-determinant domain the reduced Laplacian depends injectively on conductances of this simple graph. Off-diagonals recover nonroot edge weights, then diagonals recover root edge weights. Strict log-det concavity gives uniqueness, and polynomial invariance under intra-path permutations then forces equal weights within each path. The common weights are positive because deleting a whole long path isolates internal vertices. With path budget coordinates x_i and V=x_0+sum(c_i x_i), c_i=1/ell_i^2, the objective up to constants is sum((ell_i-1)log x_i)+log V. The stationarity multiplier is rho by summing coordinate derivatives against the allocation. If x_0 is positive, V=1/rho and x_0=(1-S)/rho; that solution also satisfies complementary slackness when S=1. On the zero-shortcut face, xi=rho V must solve sum((ell_i-1)c_i/(xi-c_i))=1 above max(c_i). This sum is strictly decreasing there and takes value S at xi=1. The root satisfies the omitted-edge inequality 1/V<=rho exactly when S>=1. The stationarity formula budgets correctly: sum((ell_i-1)xi/(xi-c_i))=sum(ell_i-1)+1=rho. Converting back gives both stated weight formulas and determinant factors, which agree at equality. The concavity argument makes the feasible KKT solution globally optimal and unique.
residual_risks: The tree-enumeration replay is finite and used floating-point bisection and products. It is corroboration; the proof covers arbitrary path lengths and budgets. The frozen SLSQP run was not rerun.

value.rationale: Uniform-cost budgeted D-optimality is a natural criterion on parallel routes. The solution predicts a support transition that a generic determinant formulation does not locate, and distinguishes threshold equality from strict deletion by the direct-edge marginal gain. The exact heterogeneous reciprocal-length rule and single-root allocation are useful beyond the previously covered cycle, short-route and book cases; they decide both whether a shortcut is worth any budget and how to allocate the rest without an edge-by-edge optimization.
residual_risks: The result does not classify heterogeneous edge prices, route intersections beyond common terminals, or other design criteria.
